sources.title: Leibniz Institute of European History: Brunswick
sources.note: Direct academic historical GIS profile, PDF pages 1 to 3: separated territory, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel name, 1807 absorption/1813 restoration, monarchy and 1832 constitutional arrangements. Imported geometry independently decoded.

sources.title: Brunswick Palace Museum: Palace history
sources.note: Direct/indexed museum narrative: 1830 citizens expelled Karl II and set palace on fire; replacement residence nineteenth century.

sources.title: Lower Saxony State Archives: The new constitution of 1832
sources.note: Direct/indexed archival collection description, STAWO 12 Neu 13 Nr. 4314 Bd. 1: October 12, 1832 hereditary monarchy and single chamber, 458 pages of drafts and deliberations. Catalog description used, not all 458 manuscript pages claimed inspected.

sources.title: Brunswick University Archives: A look into university history
sources.note: Direct university chronology: 1835 technical/commercial/humanistic departments, 1862 minimum age sixteen and subject schools, student clubs. Uses nineteenth-century entries only.

sources.title: Göttingen University Library: Carl Friedrich Gauss exhibition catalog
sources.note: Direct scholarly exhibition catalog, printed pages 11 to 12 and 22 for biography/patronage, page 164 exhibit H1 for April 8, 1803 letter to Olbers, Cod. Ms. Gauß Briefe B Olbers Nr. 29. Exact German excerpt from catalog transcription; no claim original manuscript image inspected.

sources.title: City of Brunswick: Industrial development
sources.note: Direct municipal historical account: railway 1838, sugar beets around 1850, sugar-industry school in 1870s. Conflicting agricultural reform dates elsewhere not repeated.

sources.title: City of Brunswick: Asparagus and canning
sources.note: Direct municipal account, preserving asparagus around 1850, expanded cultivation and year-round distribution. Later international shipment examples from 1881 omitted.

sources.title: City of Brunswick: The Jödebrunnen water source
sources.note: Direct municipal heritage entry, source system 1345 to 1865, wooden pipes following slope to public fountains. Earlier origin explicitly distinguished from continued nineteenth-century use.

sources.title: City of Brunswick: The former river-water works in Bürgerpark
sources.note: Direct seven-page municipal monument leaflet, printed pages 2 to 4: industrial river pollution, settling/filter basins, construction 1864, full operation January 1, 1865, 54-metre pressure tower and pipes. Later groundwater works not projected backward.

sources.title: Gerd Biegel: Franz Abt and nineteenth-century Brunswick
sources.note: Direct academic historical essay hosted by city, printed page 7 quoting a report from second half of nineteenth century: Klint housing, shared toilets, proximity of cesspits and water. Exact year not established, range may extend after imported1878; public caveat included.

sources.title: Brunswick Regional Court: The court in the Weimar Republic
sources.note: Direct court history: revolution November 8, 1918 and removal of duke, continuation as Free State, staff continuity, subsequent property dispute. Used as concrete institutional continuity.

sources.title: Historical Encyclopedia of Bavaria: The Palatinate in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries
sources.note: Direct Hans Fenske academic entry: Bavarian possession May1,1816, Speyer capital, name Pfalz from1838, revolution1849 and twentieth-century changes. Overview distinguishes province from medieval Electoral Palatinate; source public copy budgets include ending.

sources.title: City of Saarbrücken: Historical chronology
sources.note: Indexed original municipal chronology: Saarbrücken became Prussian in1815. Point-in-polygon check confirms imported Palatinate incorrectly includes Saarbrücken; public boundary warning. This source supports only identity caveat, not attribution of Saarbrücken daily life to Bavarian Pfalz.

sources.title: Historical Encyclopedia of Bavaria: Palatine regional autonomy
sources.note: Direct academic entry Pfälzischer Separatismus, section nineteenth-century special status: Code civil and self-government retained,1849 provisional government aimed at German constitutional unity rather than simple independent Palatine nation-state.

sources.title: German Historical Museum: Hambach Festival, 1832
sources.note: Direct Dorlis Blume, updatedApril5,2024: participants, explicit invitation to women, Polish flag, suppression and subsequent legal proceedings. No precise attendance total because published estimates vary.

sources.title: Hambach Castle Foundation: The Hambach flag
sources.note: Direct museum-owned object record in Google Arts and Culture:1832 flag, exact inscription Deutschlands Wiedergeburt, carried by JohannPhilippAbresch May27,1832 and raised beside Polish flag. Transcription is curator-confirmed; no new image inspection claimed.

sources.title: Historical Encyclopedia of Bavaria: Agriculture in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries
sources.note: Direct AloisSeidl academic entry: Palatinate divided inheritance unlike many OldBavarian farms. Does not project Bavarian1802schoollegislation or generalized population statistics directly onto Pfalz.

sources.title: Karsten Ruppert: The Palatinate in the Kingdom of Bavaria, 1816 to 1918
sources.note: Direct scholarly article hosted by Bavarian State Center for Political Education, page11/PDFindex10: elementary schools by confession, some community schools, Jewish schools and schoolhouses with teachers apartments. Dubious blanket total literacy claim omitted.

sources.title: KuLaDig cultural heritage: Development of the Pirmasens shoe industry
sources.note: Direct cultural-heritage account:1830mayor report150women/girls selling shoes and journey lengths, nineteenth-century Brotbücher credit system. Later paragraph incorrectly dates Vienna fair1872, so no reliance on that or later industrial totals. Early Joß origin explicitly legend in source and omitted.

sources.title: Kusel district: The tradition of traveling musicians
sources.note: Direct district tourism/museum interpretation: nineteenth-century origins, village performers, long absences, income supporting families, children learning music. Uses broad nineteenth-century scope only; no fabricated anecdotal quote or unsupported exact pre1878 global totals.

sources.title: Rhineland-Palatinate State Library Center: Acquired for the Palatinate
sources.note: Indexed original state-library exhibit:1844railwaycompany, coal transport purpose, completedAugust 1849;1854railwaytravelpublication promoted local tourism. Concrete collection witness supplies chronology.

sources.title: BASF company archive: The age of dyes
sources.note: Direct corporate chronology: company foundedMannheimApril6,1865but factory builtLudwigshafen afterlandpurchasefailedacrossriver. No claims about universal worker welfare from corporate rhetoric.

sources.title: BASF company archive: The first company physician, 1866
sources.note: Direct institutional history:1866physician. Large outpatient clinic/x-ray facilities are circa1900, not1866; public text avoids projecting them backward.

sources.title: BASF History, 1865 to 2015
sources.note: Direct59pagecorporatehistory, printed19/PDFindex10:1872Hemshofhousingconstruction,over400apartments; printed21/PDFindex11:1875company-fundedhealthbenefits.1914kitchenimageand1880housingphotographnotusedas1872roominventory.
